01 / THE STARTING POINT

Sell the feeling, not the feature list.

Wellbeing tools can add the very pressure they aim to remove. The launch film introduces Daylight in a calm forty seconds, letting the product’s tone—warm, unhurried, kind—do the talking.

Made for people looking for a little space in a busy day. The edit never rushes them.

“A calm product should feel calm in motion.”
THE EDITING PRINCIPLE
02 / THE DIRECTION

One small moment is a good place to start.

The film opens on a single interaction, then widens out gently. Soft transitions, generous holds and a warm grade keep the pace unhurried while the UI animation does the explaining.

  • Show one useful moment before a list of features.
  • Time the UI animation to real, human pauses.
  • Let the music and the interface breathe together.

Warm / Unhurried

Clear, friendly titles and soft contrast keep the film welcoming. A restrained grade keeps the product UI accurate and consistent with the app.

03 / THE EDIT

A clear path.
A distinct feeling.

Open, check in, choose a small moment. The film follows the same simple path as the app, so the story and the product promise match.

WHAT THE FILM BRINGS TOGETHER

Edit & structure

A forty-second narrative built around one daily ritual.

UI animation

Screen recordings, animated interface moments and device mockups.

Grade & finish

A warm, consistent grade with exports for every platform.

04 / THE TAKEAWAY

A note for
the next cut.

The most useful editing decision was subtraction. Removing pressure and keeping the first moment simple made the whole film feel more approachable.

This is an independent concept. It presents the intended edit and visual direction, rather than results from a commissioned campaign.
